title: 250. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Vertical Line Test
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Purpose of the Vertical Line Test
questions.learningObjective: Identify what the vertical line test determines about a graph.
questions.question: What does the vertical line test determine about a graph in the \(xy\)-plane?

options.label: A
options.text: Whether the graph is symmetric about the \(y\)-axis

options.label: B
options.text: Whether the graph represents \(y\) as a function of \(x\)

questions.explanation: The vertical line test checks whether any vertical line intersects the graph at more than one point. If every vertical line intersects the graph at most once, then each \(x\)-value has at most one corresponding \(y\)-value, so the graph represents \(y\) as a function of \(x\). Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Recall the condition that a function must assign at most one output to each input.

questions.concept: Interpreting a Failed Vertical Line Test
questions.learningObjective: Determine the conclusion when a vertical line intersects a graph more than once.
questions.question: A vertical line intersects a graph at two distinct points. What does this imply about the graph?

options.label: A
options.text: The graph represents \(y\) as a function of \(x\).

options.label: B
options.text: The graph does not represent \(y\) as a function of \(x\).

questions.explanation: If a vertical line intersects the graph at two distinct points, then one \(x\)-value corresponds to two different \(y\)-values. This violates the definition of a function. Therefore the graph does not represent \(y\) as a function of \(x\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Check whether one input value is paired with more than one output value.

questions.concept: Applying the Vertical Line Test to a Circle
questions.learningObjective: Use the vertical line test to decide whether a circle represents a function.
questions.question: The graph of \(x^2+y^2=25\) is a circle. Does this graph represent \(y\) as a function of \(x\)?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, because every \(x\)-value gives exactly one \(y\)-value.

options.label: B
options.text: No, because the vertical line \(x=0\) intersects the circle at \((0,5)\) and \((0,-5)\).

questions.explanation: For \(x=0\), the equation gives \(y^2=25\), so \(y=5\) or \(y=-5\). Thus the vertical line \(x=0\) intersects the graph at two points. The graph fails the vertical line test, so it does not represent \(y\) as a function of \(x\). Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Substitute a convenient \(x\)-value and see whether it produces more than one \(y\)-value.

questions.concept: Applying the Vertical Line Test to a Horizontal Parabola
questions.learningObjective: Use the vertical line test to decide whether \(x=y^2\) represents a function.
questions.question: The graph of \(x=y^2\) is a parabola opening to the right. Does this graph represent \(y\) as a function of \(x\)?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, because it is a parabola.

options.label: B
options.text: No, because the vertical line \(x=4\) intersects the graph at \((4,2)\) and \((4,-2)\).

questions.explanation: For \(x=4\), the equation gives \(4=y^2\), so \(y=2\) or \(y=-2\). The vertical line \(x=4\) intersects the graph at two points. Therefore the graph fails the vertical line test and does not represent \(y\) as a function of \(x\). Hence option B is correct.
questions.hint: Choose a positive \(x\)-value and solve for \(y\) to see whether two outputs occur.

questions.concept: Applying the Vertical Line Test to an Upward Parabola
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether \(y=x^2\) passes the vertical line test.
questions.question: The graph of \(y=x^2\) is a parabola opening upward. Does this graph pass the vertical line test?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, because every vertical line intersects the graph at most once.

options.label: B
options.text: No, because every vertical line intersects the graph twice.

questions.explanation: For any real number \(x\), the equation \(y=x^2\) gives exactly one \(y\)-value. Therefore every vertical line intersects the graph at most once. The graph passes the vertical line test, so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Check whether any single \(x\)-value can produce two different \(y\)-values.

questions.concept: Applying the Vertical Line Test to a Vertical Line
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a vertical line represents \(y\) as a function of \(x\).
questions.question: The graph is the vertical line \(x=2\). Does this graph represent \(y\) as a function of \(x\)?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, because \(x\) is constant.

options.label: B
options.text: No, because the vertical line \(x=2\) intersects the graph at infinitely many points.

questions.explanation: The graph \(x=2\) contains all points of the form \((2,y)\). The vertical line \(x=2\) therefore intersects the graph at infinitely many points, so one \(x\)-value corresponds to many \(y\)-values. The graph fails the vertical line test and is not a function of \(x\). Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Count how many points of the graph lie on the vertical line \(x=2\).

questions.concept: Applying the Vertical Line Test to a Horizontal Line
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a horizontal line passes the vertical line test.
questions.question: The graph is the horizontal line \(y=3\). Does this graph pass the vertical line test?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, because every vertical line intersects the graph exactly once.

options.label: B
options.text: No, because some vertical lines intersect the graph more than once.

questions.explanation: For every real number \(x\), the graph has exactly one point \((x,3)\). Thus every vertical line intersects the graph exactly once. The graph passes the vertical line test, so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Check how many points the graph has for any chosen \(x\)-value.

questions.concept: Applying the Vertical Line Test to an Upper Semicircle
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether an upper semicircle passes the vertical line test.
questions.question: The graph is the upper semicircle \(y=\sqrt{9-x^2}\). Does this graph pass the vertical line test?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, because each vertical line intersects the graph at most once.

options.label: B
options.text: No, because each vertical line intersects the graph twice.

questions.explanation: For each \(x\) in the domain \(-3\le x\le 3\), the expression \(\sqrt{9-x^2}\) gives exactly one nonnegative \(y\)-value. Outside this domain there is no point on the graph. Therefore every vertical line intersects the graph at most once, so it passes the vertical line test. Hence option A is correct.
questions.hint: Decide how many values \(\sqrt{9-x^2}\) can have for one allowed \(x\)-value.

questions.concept: Applying the Vertical Line Test to an Absolute Value Graph
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether the graph of \(y=|x|\) represents a function.
questions.question: The graph of \(y=|x|\) is a V-shaped graph. Does this graph represent \(y\) as a function of \(x\)?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, because every vertical line intersects the graph at most once.

options.label: B
options.text: No, because every vertical line intersects the graph twice.

questions.explanation: For any real number \(x\), the absolute value \(|x|\) is a single nonnegative number. Therefore each \(x\)-value gives exactly one \(y\)-value, and every vertical line intersects the graph at most once. The graph represents \(y\) as a function of \(x\), so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Check whether the definition of absolute value can ever produce two outputs for the same input.

questions.concept: General Criterion from the Vertical Line Test
questions.learningObjective: Select the correct conclusion from the vertical line test.
questions.question: Which statement is a correct conclusion from the vertical line test?

options.label: A
options.text: If every vertical line intersects a graph at most once, then the graph represents \(y\) as a function of \(x\).

options.label: B
options.text: If some vertical line intersects a graph at most once, then the graph represents \(y\) as a function of \(x\).

questions.explanation: The vertical line test requires checking every vertical line. A graph represents \(y\) as a function of \(x\) only when every vertical line intersects the graph at most once. If only some vertical line intersects at most once, another vertical line might still intersect the graph more than once. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Recall how many vertical lines the test requires you to check.
